title: BPP execution_permit_consume result (DESIGN.md §13.1, §14.8; registry R34 runtime)
description: Success.result for execution_permit_consume: the verbatim §13.1 ExecutionConsumptionReceipt with max_uses pinned to 1 (one-shot; gap note G37, G4 invariant-pinning precedent). If the host crashes after consumption it recovers this same receipt rather than asking for new authority; the host intersects it with stricter current platform policy, mints its local permit, and only then creates a driver attempt (§13.1 steps 6–7). Episode binding on the receipt is an exact pair: episode_ref with episode_fence_digest, both-or-neither (RT-05). EVERY member this shape defines is RENDERED — a digest member returned as null is a conformance failure, never an omission the consumer may treat as a match (kovee seam finding on the receipt, gap note G48). Each digest is one the consumer can actually check, per member (A8, PROFILE.md §6.2, R3-L01). intent_digest, subject_digest and episode_fence_digest are byom's OWN committed record digests: they stay local_erasure_safe, they are NOT request members any more — byom recomputes each from its committed ActIntent, act subject and ByomEpisodeBinding rather than asking the consumer to echo a value it holds no key for — and they are published here so the consumer can carry them in its own audit. disclosure_digest is the HOST's own object, so it is portable_public, and the value rendered is the one the act was AUTHORIZED for, read from byom's committed act subject: a consumption presenting a different pair is refused, never copied (R3-A01). mandate_use_digest and digest name records the consumer never supplied and holds no key for, so they are portable_public over frozen cross-boundary fragments the consumer re-derives.

mandate_use_digest.description: The CROSS-BOUNDARY pin of the MandateUse this consumption inserted (A8; the resource_allocation_digest construction, gap note G48). The consumer never supplied a MandateUse and holds no per-object secret for byom's own mandate_uses.digest, so a keyed class here would be an opaque blob it could only echo. This is portable_public SHA-256 over the $domain-tagged canonical bytes of exactly the frozen `bpp-mandate-use-binding-v0` fragment {mandate_use_id, intent_ref, use_key, consumed_at}, whose every member is published on this receipt: mandate_use_id is mandate_use_ref, intent_ref is intent_ref, use_key is stable_execution_key, consumed_at is issued_at. byom's own local_erasure_safe MandateUse record commitment is unchanged and is demanded from nobody.

disclosure_digest.description: The disclosure manifest this act was AUTHORIZED for, read from byom's committed act subject — never the value the consumption carried (R3-A01). The host owns the manifest and byom cannot re-derive its content, so the class is portable_public (A8): both sides hold the same bytes and the broker compares it with the manifest it staged.

max_uses.description: Invariant constant: an ExecutionConsumptionReceipt is one-shot (§13.1).

digest.description: The receipt's own CROSS-BOUNDARY commitment (A8): portable_public SHA-256 over the $domain-tagged canonical bytes of the frozen `bpp-execution-consumption-receipt-binding-v0` fragment — EXACTLY the members of this shape except `digest` itself, with an absent optional binding ABSENT (never null) and the transport-only `replayed` marker excluded. The consumer therefore derives it from the receipt it just received, which is the whole point: it is the one digest that authenticates the binding the broker relies on before egress, so it can never be a keyed value only byom can compute. The keyed member digests inside this preimage are published bytes both sides hold, not values the consumer must derive, so PROFILE.md §6.2's public-hash prohibition is untouched: erasing an object secret still erases exactly that member's own verifiability, while this pin only ever proved the receipt's bytes are the bytes byom committed. byom keeps no keyed twin — nothing inside byom compares this value; it exists to cross the boundary.

identifier.description: Opaque visible-ASCII identifier, at most 128 bytes (§14.9).

safeNonNegativeInteger.description: I-JSON safe integer (§14.2 rejects unsafe integers).

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant with Z offset, semantically valid in the proleptic Gregorian calendar: the pattern pins the lexical ranges and implementations MUST additionally reject impossible calendar instants (e.g. 2026-02-30) — the conformance runner enforces this on every vector; leap seconds are not accepted. DESIGN.md does not fix a timestamp wire encoding; this derivation freezes with the bundle (gap note G3, amended per RT-17).

digestRef.$comment: The closed family DigestRef wire (family-vectors/PROFILE.md §6.1, normative; D-R0-1): exactly the members {class, algorithm, key_ref?, value_hex}. The oneOf pins the closed class/algorithm pairing and requires key_ref exactly for the keyed erasure classes; each arm refines members of this already-closed object.

class.description: Digest class (PROFILE.md §6, D-R0-1); substituting one class where a schema requires another is a conformance failure.

key_ref.description: Key id for the keyed erasure classes; raw HMAC keys, per-object secrets, and salts are never part of a DigestRef.

digestRef.description: Typed DigestRef: every digest field is typed, never an unlabelled hash. Wire shape, class/algorithm pairing, and key_ref presence per the ratified family profile.

localErasureSafeDigest.description: Contextual digest-class binding (PROFILE.md §6.2, D-R0-1; RT-02): this field commits to an authority subject or other erasable per-object content, so exactly class local_erasure_safe (per-object secret, keyed HMAC) is acceptable. A well-constructed digest of any other class here is digest_class_mismatch — never a silent substitution.

portableBindingDigest.description: Contextual digest-class binding (PROFILE.md §6.2 cross-boundary class rule, amendment §A8; RT-02): this field commits to a FROZEN cross-boundary fragment the consumer holds and must re-derive without a byom secret, so exactly class portable_public (unkeyed SHA-256 over the $domain-tagged canonical fragment) is acceptable. A well-constructed digest of any other class here is digest_class_mismatch — and a keyed one would be a value the consumer could only echo, which is the defect the rule exists to prevent.
